parts:
Hi:

If you can live with both bars in the Overall group being the same color, it's not too difficult. Here's one way. (BTW, thank you for presenting code and a picture of what you're after - it's very helpful. The data...meh. dput(dataframe) would have been ideal.)

Given your data is read in,

# Reorder the factor levels
maternity.score.long$id <- ordered(maternity.score.long$id, levels = c(
  'Overall', 'K/Mposhi', 'Kitwe', 'Katete', 'Nchelenge', 'Lusaka',
  'Mwinilunga', 'Livingstone', 'Sesheke'))

# Add indicators for Overall and 'not Overall' - the idea is to make two geom_bar()
# plots, one for Overall, to which we set a color, and another geom_bar() for the
# non-Overall data, using your previous code.

maternity.score.long <- transform(maternity.score.long,
      m1 = rep(c(rep(1, 8), 0), 2), m2 = 1 - rep(c(rep(1, 8), 0), 2) )

# Use ggplot() to combine the two plots as layers:

g <- ggplot(maternity.score.long, aes(x = id))
g + geom_bar(aes(y = m1 * value, fill = variable),
             stat = 'identity', position = 'dodge', width = 0.6) +
    geom_bar(aes(y = m2 * value), fill = 'orange',
             stat = 'identity', position = 'dodge', width = 0.6) +
    theme_bw() + xlab("") + ylab('Score') + ylim(0, 100) +
scale_fill_manual("",values=c("powderblue","violet")) +

geom_text(aes(y = value + 0.2,
                 label = format(maternity.score.long$value,
                          digits=1, nsmall=0), hjust=hjust),
                          colour="black", vjust=-0.4, size=3) +

opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-45, hjust=0),
        title="Density score 2008 & 2010")

Setting the fill color in the second call to geom_bar() simplifies matters immensely.

The problem with having different colors for the bars in the Overall group is that you need to map a variable for fill color. By doing that, you will by default be adding those colors to the legend, which you don't want, but you'd need another fill_scale_manual() call to assign yellow and orange to the values for that variable and set legend = FALSE correctly. If someone else wants to have a go at that, please do. I tried two scale_fill_manual() calls (no dice - the second one overwrites the first, as expected), and set up two individual plots in the hope I could 'add' them together - that didn't work, either. I thought the second idea might have a chance, actually; here's what I tried:

# Need the ordered factors as in the above code - don't forget :)

maternity.score.long <- transform(maternity.score.long,
      m1 = rep(c(rep(1, 8), 0), 2), m2 = 1 - rep(c(rep(1, 8), 0), 2),
      gp = rep(c('A', 'B'), each = 9))     # add a character var (could be a factor, too...)

# First plot without the Overall group:
g <- ggplot(maternity.score.long, aes(x = id, fill = variable))
g0 <- g + geom_bar(aes(y = m1 * value, fill = variable),
             stat = 'identity', position = 'dodge', width = 0.6) +
    theme_bw() + xlab("") + ylab('Score') + ylim(0, 100) +
scale_fill_manual("",values=c("powderblue","violet")) +

geom_text(aes(y = value + 0.2,
                 label = format(maternity.score.long$value,
                          digits=1, nsmall=0), hjust=hjust),
                          colour="black", vjust=-0.4, size=3) +

opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-45, hjust=0),
        title="Density score 2008 & 2010")

# Second plot with the Overall group only:
h <- ggplot(maternity.score.long, aes(x = id, fill = gp)) 
h0 <- h +  geom_bar(aes(y = m2 * value),
             stat = 'identity', position = 'dodge', width = 0.6) +
     scale_fill_manual("", values = c('yellow', 'orange'), legend = FALSE) +
     theme_bw() + xlab("") + ylab('Score') + ylim(0, 100) +
     geom_text(aes(y = value + 0.2,
                 label = format(maternity.score.long$value,
                          digits=1, nsmall=0), hjust=hjust),
                          colour="black", vjust=-0.4, size=3) +

opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-45, hjust=0),
        title="Density score 2008 & 2010")

# Superimpose?  Alas, no...
h0 + g0


If there's a way to pull this off, I'd love to see it.  Is rock star Hadley in the house?  :)  *

HTH,
Dennis

My first thought was that the fill colour is controlled by the
interaction of the "variable" column and whether it is the overall
group (id=="Overall"), so why not set that explicitly.

geom_bar(aes(y = value, fill = interaction(variable,id=="Overall")),

values=c("powderblue","violet","yellow","orange"),
labels=c("GM2008","SAM2001","","")) +

label = format(maternity.score.long$value,
digits=1, nsmall=0), hjust=hjust),
colour="black", vjust=-0.4, size=3) +
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-45, hjust=0),
title="Density score 2008 & 2010")

This is almost there, except there are entries in the legend for the
Overall bars (at least color boxes; the labels have been blanked
out). I thought limits might help, but by limiting the scale to just
the non-overall groups, the overall group is dropped (as is consistent
for ggplot; data points outside the imposed limits of a scale are
dropped). I don't know of any way to force a legend to only show
certain values rather than limit the data to them (somewhat analogous
to coord_cartesian(xlim=...) which limits what part of the x-axis is
shown, even though it does not limit the data used).

I got something to work, but it is VERY hackish, and I feel like I'm
subverting mechanisms rather than using them properly. In other words,
I can do it, but I won't say I'm proud of how I did it ;)

ggplot(maternity.score.long, aes(x = id)) +
geom_bar(aes(y = value, fill = variable),
data=maternity.score.long[maternity.score.long$id != "Overall",],
stat = 'identity', position = 'dodge', width = 0.6) +

geom_bar(aes(x=as.numeric(id)-0.2, y = value, width=0.4),
fill = 'yellow',
data=maternity.score.long[maternity.score.long$id == "Overall" &
maternity.score.long$variable == "GF2008",],
stat = 'identity') +
geom_bar(aes(x=as.numeric(id)+0.2, y = value, width=0.4),
fill = 'orange',
data=maternity.score.long[maternity.score.long$id == "Overall" &
maternity.score.long$variable == "SAM2010",],
stat = 'identity') +

theme_bw() + xlab("") + ylab('Score') + ylim(0, 100) +
scale_fill_manual("",values=c("powderblue","violet")) +
geom_text(aes(y = value + 0.2,
label = format(maternity.score.long$value,
digits=1, nsmall=0), hjust=hjust),
colour="black", vjust=-0.4, size=3) +
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-45, hjust=0),
title="Density score 2008 & 2010")

Basically, I put each of the yellow and orange bars in separately,
manually dodging (by adjusting the x coordinate) and adjusting their
width. Also, I subset the data using the data argument rather than
multiplying by indicator variables like Dennis did. Either way works
and is a matter of taste. The yellow and orange bars might be a touch
narrower than the others (it's close but I can't quite tell); you can
adjust them by changing the offset in the ase(x=...) and the width
there as well. The width should be twice the offset so that they will
touch.

Overall bars (at least color boxes; the labels have been blanked
out).  I thought limits might help, but by limiting the scale to just
the non-overall groups, the overall group is dropped (as is consistent
for ggplot; data points outside the imposed limits of a scale are
dropped).  I don't know of any way to force a legend to only show
certain values rather than limit the data to them (somewhat analogous
to coord_cartesian(xlim=...) which limits what part of the x-axis is
shown, even though it does not limit the data used).

I got something to work, but it is VERY hackish, and I feel like I'm
subverting mechanisms rather than using them properly. In other words,
I can do it, but I won't say I'm proud of how I did it ;)

 geom_bar(aes(y = value, fill = variable),

   fill = 'orange',
   data=maternity.score.long[maternity.score.long$id == "Overall" &
maternity.score.long$variable == "SAM2010",],
   stat = 'identity') +
 theme_bw() + xlab("") + ylab('Score') + ylim(0, 100) +
 scale_fill_manual("",values=c("powderblue","violet")) +
  geom_text(aes(y = value + 0.2,
                label = format(maternity.score.long$value,
                         digits=1, nsmall=0), hjust=hjust),
                         colour="black", vjust=-0.4, size=3) +
  opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-45, hjust=0),
       title="Density score 2008 & 2010")

Basically, I put each of the yellow and orange bars in separately,
manually dodging (by adjusting the x coordinate) and adjusting their
width.  Also, I subset the data using the data argument rather than
multiplying by indicator variables like Dennis did.  Either way works
and is a matter of taste.  The yellow and orange bars might be a touch
narrower than the others (it's close but I can't quite tell); you can
adjust them by changing the offset in the ase(x=...) and the width
there as well.  The width should be twice the offset so that they will
touch.
